3. Write the correct answer and three plausible but demonstrably wrong answers.
   Verify each choice against the unchanged stem. If two work, change the item.
4. Give a brief explanation consistent with the final stem and answer. Return

letters, all/none-of-the-above options, duplicate JSON keys, or options in the stem.

- uncertain: you cannot establish support or refutation, for example because

items.prompt: A passenger wants to travel from Harbor to Ridge on Wednesday. What is the minimum number of lines they must use?
choices: No solution exists under the stated conditions.

items.prompt: On which day can a passenger travel from Park to Harbor using exactly two different lines?
choices: No solution exists under the stated conditions.

choices.reason: No single line connects Harbor to Ridge directly. Harbor is on Copper (Harbor-Market), Ridge is on Silver (Market-Ridge) and Gold (Ridge-Park). No single line spans Harbor to Ridge.

Harbor→Market via Copper, then Market→Ridge via Silver. On Wednesday, Copper runs (Mon/Wed/Fri) but Silver runs only Monday and Friday—not Wednesday. Harbor→Market via Copper then Ridge via Silver is impossible Wednesday. No other two-line path exists. So two lines cannot be done on Wednesday either, making this refuted.

Only three lines exist total (Copper, Silver, Gold). A three-line path Harbor→Market(Copper)→Ridge(Silver)→Park(Gold)→Ridge(Gold) would revisit stations and is not a valid minimum. No three-line simple path from Harbor to Ridge exists meaningfully.

choices.choice: No solution exists under the stated conditions.
choices.reason: On Wednesday, Copper runs but Silver does not (Silver runs Mon/Fri only). The only route Harbor→Ridge requires Copper then Silver. Since Silver doesn't run Wednesday, no journey from Harbor to Ridge is possible on Wednesday.

Park→Ridge via Gold (runs Mon? No—Gold runs Wed/Fri), then Ridge→Market via Silver (runs Mon/Fri), then Market→Harbor via Copper (runs Mon/Wed/Fri). On Friday: Gold runs, Silver runs, Copper runs—valid. On Monday: Gold does NOT run (Gold runs Wed/Fri only), so Monday fails. Friday works but need to check if it's the only day.

choices.choice: No solution exists under the stated conditions.
choices.reason: On Friday, Park→Ridge (Gold, runs Fri) then Ridge→Market (Silver, runs Fri) then Market→Harbor (Copper, runs Fri) gives a three-line journey, not two. The only two-line path Park→Ridge(Gold)→Market? No, Silver goes Market-Ridge. Two lines: Gold(Park-Ridge) + Silver(Ridge-Market) gets to Market not Harbor. Need a third line Copper for Harbor. So exactly two lines cannot reach Harbor from Park.
On Monday, Gold does not run (Gold runs Wed/Fri). Park connects only via Gold to Ridge. Without Gold, Park is unreachable, so no journey from Park is possible Monday.

On Wednesday, Gold runs (Park→Ridge), but Silver does not run (Silver runs Mon/Fri). Cannot proceed Ridge→Market. So Wednesday fails too. In fact no two-line journey from Park to Harbor exists on any day since the path requires three lines minimum.
